label: Foundational beings are contingent at w, from Kant's thesis and concept adequacy
description: A second support bundle for the 'possibly absent' verdict, beside the existence-conditional one (872a3832): Kant's conceptual thesis extended, by concept adequacy, to a concept adequate to the nature replaces existence-conditional essences and the representability premise. Not a transcription: no premise mentions contingency. Establishes no premise. Each premise is needed (controls, Kant-adequacy omissions 1-4); nonvacuous (controls, conditionalIdentity). The two concept premises must hold of one concept relation: adequacy fails for a concept formed only from a being's effects (controls, kantAquinas), so the argument needs Kant's thesis to govern a concept adequate to the nature, which is the disputed extension at an esse-essence identity (docs/notes/existence-in-essence-identity.md).
